metadata.case_name: KWOK HANG KEI v. QUON HING CONCRETE CO LTD AND OTHERS

plaintiff.occupation_after: site clerk (clerical position with 1st Defendant since October 1987)

injuries.description: Fractured right clavicle and multiple abrasions over both hands, shoulders and both knees.
injuries.body_part: right clavicle; both hands; shoulders; both knees
source: (4) Fractured right clavicle and multiple abrasions over both hands, shoulders and both knees.

injuries.description: Fractured d shaft of the left femur initially treated by nailing but later changed to external fixation because of collapse over the fracture site even with nail in situ.
source: (2) Fractured d shaft of the left femur initially treated by nailing but later changed to external fixation because of collapse over the fracture site even with nail in situ.

injuries.description: Multiple abrasions over both hands, shoulders and both knees.
source: (4) Fractured right clavicle and multiple abrasions over both hands, shoulders and both knees.

injuries.description: Serious cosmetic disability with scars over left leg, right buttock and leg, right and left arms and trunk; scars will always remain conspicuous and ugly; plastic surgery cannot significantly lessen degree of cosmetic disability.
injuries.body_part: left leg; right buttock and leg; right and left arms; trunk
source: Dr. Ian Nicolson in his report and accompanying colour photographs was satisfied the Plaintiff had serious cosmetic disability over his left leg, right buttock and leg, right and left arms and his trunk, and that although the scars will improve a little with time, the ugly scars will always remain conspicuous and ugly. In this opinion of Dr. Nicholson plastic surgery cannot significantly lessen the Plaintiff's degree of cosmetic disability.

injuries.description: Multiple fractures of the left foot resulting in a syme amputation of the left foot at the ankle.
injuries.body_part: left foot at the ankle (syme amputation)
source: (1) Multiple fractures of the left foot resulting in a syme amputation of the left foot at the ankle.
injuries.icd_description: Traumatic amputation of left foot at ankle level

injuries.description: Amputation of the 4th toe of the right foot.
source: (3) Amputation of the 4th toe of the right foot.

injuries.description: Serious depression requiring active supportive psychiatric treatment over a protracted period.
source: Dr. William Green in his psychiatric reports on the Plaintiff reached the conclusion that he was seriously depressed and required active supportive psychiatric treatment over a protracted period.

manifestations.description: Suffers from headaches especially when reading.
The Plaintiff had seven operations in Princess Margaret Hospital and was discharged after 10 months in July 1987.
The Plaintiff wears a prosthesis in place of his amputated left foot which will have to be changed every 2 years.
Ugly scars will always remain conspicuous and ugly (serious cosmetic disability).
Seriously depressed and requiring active supportive psychiatric treatment over a protracted period.
52% permanent disability and loss of earning capacity (as assessed in the Employee Compensation proceedings).

treatments_received: Seven operations in Princess Margaret Hospital
Wears a prosthesis in place of his amputated left foot which will have to be changed every 2 years
treatments_future: Replacement prosthesis for left foot every 2 years
Psychotherapy / psychiatric treatment (Dr. W. Green evidence that the Plaintiff requires psychotherapy treatment for up to 2 years)

losses.description: Amputations and fractures including syme amputation of left foot, amputation of 4th toe of right foot, fractured left femur and fractured right clavicle resulting in loss/impairment of bodily integrity.
Serious cosmetic disability: conspicuous and ugly scars over left leg, right buttock and leg, right and left arms and trunk; plastic surgery cannot significantly lessen the cosmetic disability.
Dr. William Green in his psychiatric reports on the Plaintiff reached the conclusion that he was seriously depressed and required active supportive psychiatric treatment over a protracted period.
